assessment.nobel_worthiness: A foundational body of work that supplied the central framework for modern monetary-policy analysis.
assessment.attribution: Calvo, Taylor and Woodford provide a coherent and individually identifiable core, though the listed contribution has many essential contributors.
assessment.maturity: The framework has guided theory, empirical work and policy institutions for decades.
uncertainties: The candidate's broad credit set makes a three-person attribution necessarily incomplete.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The analysis of collateral constraints and amplification transformed macro-finance and understanding of financial crises.
assessment.attribution: Kiyotaki and Moore supply the seminal collateral mechanism, with Gertler central to its financial-accelerator development.
assessment.maturity: Its consequences have been extensively developed and tested, particularly since the global financial crisis.
uncertainties: The precise boundary between the collateral and financial-accelerator contributions is difficult to compress into three laureates.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Their work made intertemporal open-economy macroeconomics a disciplined framework for studying exchange rates and international adjustment.
assessment.attribution: Obstfeld and Rogoff are the clear central pair for the stated contribution.
assessment.maturity: The research has had long-standing influence across international macroeconomics and policy debate.
uncertainties: Exchange-rate puzzles remain only partly resolved, complicating assessment of the framework's empirical closure.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: This work substantially changed macroeconomic analysis of distribution, household balance sheets and policy transmission.
assessment.attribution: Kaplan, Moll and Violante form a well-defined core for the heterogeneous-agent New Keynesian contribution.
assessment.maturity: The approach is now influential in policy analysis and has generated a large research program.
uncertainties: Relative to older macroeconomic frameworks, its ultimate empirical and policy record is still developing.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The work gave political economy rigorous tools for analyzing institutions, electoral incentives and fiscal capacity.
assessment.attribution: Persson, Tabellini and Besley are major and complementary architects of the modern field.
assessment.maturity: The literature is mature, broadly applied and influential in both theory and empirical institutional analysis.
uncertainties: The contribution spans several related institutional mechanisms rather than one sharply bounded discovery.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The quantitative analysis of misallocation provided a powerful account of productivity and income differences across economies.
assessment.attribution: Hsieh, Klenow and Restuccia have closely connected and clearly recognizable contributions to this program.
assessment.maturity: The framework has been widely used and has stimulated extensive measurement and policy research.
uncertainties: Inference from measured wedges to underlying distortions remains model-dependent.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Their work extended economic analysis to exhaustible natural capital, biodiversity and intergenerational wealth.
assessment.attribution: Dasgupta and Heal are central pioneers of the stated environmental-economics contribution.
assessment.maturity: The ideas are longstanding and increasingly consequential for environmental accounting and policy.
uncertainties: Valuing biodiversity and inclusive wealth entails substantial measurement and normative uncertainty.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Their long-run evidence on crises, debt and default reshaped comparative historical analysis of financial instability.
assessment.attribution: Reinhart and Rogoff are the identifiable joint leaders of the stated research program.
assessment.maturity: The work has had sustained scholarly and policy influence over many years.
uncertainties: Historical-data construction and interpretation are contested, and causal conclusions are not always decisive.
